text:
Alex: Quick sync — I'm doing a short spike on internal routing choices. Thinking proto-driven route descriptors + a JSON-friendly gateway. Anyone object?
Maria: no objection. proto-driven routes make telemetry and contract checks much cleaner. gRPC streaming is tempting for KV cache & low-latency tails.
Kevin: my worry is client ergonomics. Browser + mobile SDKs hate grpc-web setup. We can't force every integration to carry grpc tooling.
Priya: what about a translator front that accepts JSON and routes to gRPC backends? Keeps clients simple, gives us typed contracts internally. Need to think about quotas and cost attribution though.
Alex: agreed. laying out options succinctly:
- Option A: gRPC internal (typed) + JSON edge translator (transcode at gateway)
- Option B: REST/JSON everywhere, encode protobufs in bodies for typing
- Option C: Dual-stack (per-route toggle) with gradual rollouts
Maria: A = best perf, B = simplest for clients, C = most flexible but operationally heavy. We should decide based on rollout risk & telemetry coverage.
Kevin: telemetry is critical. We need per-route, per-tenant token counts, backend-variant, and latency histograms. Console must expose the rollout signal (latency/cost/error) and a fast rollback.
Priya: also need to capture fallback rates when gateway fails to transcode and we fall back to a slower path. That's a key signal for canary.
Alex: question: who performs transcoding? central gateway or sidecar per node? Central gateway simplifies logic but is a CPU hotspot. Sidecar distributes CPU but complicates deployment.
Maria: sidecar + local cache hints seems attractive. sidecar can do prefix/KV cache hints to reduce repeated decode work. And we avoid a single gateway bottleneck.
Kevin: streaming / upload flows are another headache. grpc-stream maps poorly to browser chunked JSON. We probably need chunked endpoints or a separate REST upload proxy.
Priya: operational constraints: canaries should be per-tenant and per-route. Rollout signals: 95p latency spike, error-rate >2%, cost-per-token delta >10%. Those should auto-stop rollout.
Alex: rough config sketch (proto-driven route descriptor):
```
routes:
  - name: generate
    accept: application/json
    backend: grpc://inference.prod
    proto: models.generate.v1
    quota_key: tenant_id
    rollout:
      strategy: tenant-canary
      shards: 100
```
Maria: love the descriptor. Console UX idea: "Route inspector" where you can click a route and see live telemetry (latency, token cost, fallback rate), sample requests, and a one-click rollback to previous backend variant.
Kevin: also add "estimated token cost" in the preview UI so engineers see cost impact before enabling traffic. Helps with cost-aware rollouts.
Priya: telemetry proto I'll draft will include fields: route_id, tenant_id, backend_variant, tokens, processing_ms, fallback_reason, quota_bucket. I'll add enums for variant and fallback_reason. @Alex can you add a sample event shape?
Alex: yup, I'll push a draft in the spike repo. Action items:
- Priya: telemetry proto + sample events (ETA 2d)
- Kevin: prototype JSON->gRPC translator perf numbers (ETA 3d)
- Maria: mockup console Route Inspector (ETA 4d)
- Alex: prototype sidecar transcoder spike and measure CPU impact (ETA 5d)
sre-bot: NOTE: created spike ticket INF-842, link: https://go/repo/INF-842 :memo:
Maria: sweet. one more thought — quotas: we need shardable quota keys to avoid hot tenants. use hashed quota_bucket derived from tenant_id.
Kevin: +1. also expose quota consumption in console per time-window.
Priya: drafting telemetry now. I'll ping in this thread with proto link.
Alex: thanks team. short, focused spike — keep messages in this thread for traceability. :thumbsup:
